_comment: The first twenty predicaments of ADVENTURES.md §6.7 (C.6). roles: how each is bound (situations.BINDS: root, job, notable, watch, priest, healer, merchant, any, kin, tie, stranger, band, site, threat, figure, far; `or` a second way). The one who asks is the role 'asker'. obstacles: what stands in the way, each with its acts (with the role `who`: a check, a price, needs/unless conditions, then ops) and the spells that pass it. goals: goals.py tests; endings: the first whose `when` goal is reached and whose `if` holds; lapse: the world's own outcome when the clock runs out. Money is in copper (100 = 1 gp).

note: {lost} is out at {band_site}, with {band}.
{band} keep {lost} at {band_site}.

label: Where would {lost} go? Tell me everything.
say: To {band}. Out at {band_site}. Everyone knows where they sleep, and nobody goes.
{band}. They came to the market with coin and stories, and {lost} listened. They are at {band_site}.
note: {asker} says {lost} went to {band} at {band_site}.

line: {lost} is home, thin and quiet, and {asker} will not let go of {lost_them}.
{lost} sleeps under {asker}'s roof again. Nobody in the house speaks of {band}.
{lost} stays. It is not easy, but {lost_they} stays.
{lost} is alive, and gone again by the next new moon. {asker} lights a candle in the window anyway.
Alive, but not home: {lost} went back to the road. It was {lost_their} own choice.
{lost} is dead. {asker} buried {lost_them} by the temple wall.
They brought {lost} home on a door. {asker} has not spoken since.
{lost} rode out with {band} and did not come back. There is a new grave by the temple.
Nobody went for {lost}. Word came at last from {band_site}: there is a grave in {town} now.

title: {asker}'s {lost_kin}
Gone to {band}
The road to {band_site}
plea: My {lost_kin}, {lost}. {lost_they} went to {band}, out at {band_site}. I know what they do to the ones who want to leave. Bring {lost_them} home. Please.
{lost} is gone. Gone to {band}. {lost_they} thinks they are friends. They are not. I cannot go out there - but you could.
first: {asker} of {town} begged me to bring {lost_their} {lost_kin} {lost} home from {band} at {band_site}.

promise_unkept.name: A promise that cannot be kept

note: {asker} owes {creditor_full} {price_pay}, and cannot pay {by_due}.

label: I will pay what {asker} owes.
say: Well. Well, well. Paid in full. Tell {asker} the slate is clean.
Coin is coin. It's done, then.

label: Give {asker} until the harvest. You lose nothing by waiting.
say: ...Until the harvest. Not a day more.
Fine. Fine! But I'll have it with the harvest.
fail_say: A promise is a promise. I'll have it {due} or I'll have the house.

label: Forget this debt, or answer to me.
say: ...Forget it, then. Forget it! Just go.
All right! All right. It's forgotten.
fail_say: Threaten me in my own house? Get out before I call the watch.

line: {asker}'s promise is kept with your coin. {asker} will not forget it.
The debt is paid. {asker} wept, and then laughed, and then wept again.
The debt is gone, but {creditor} will not forget who frightened it away.
{creditor} gave up the debt. {asker} is free of it, and {creditor} crosses the street to avoid you.
Broken, but with honour: {asker} has until the harvest.
{creditor} will wait. It is not an end, but it is time.
{asker} could not pay. {creditor} has taken what there was, and {asker}'s door is shut.
The day came and went. {asker} broke the promise, and the town knows it.

title: {asker}'s debt
What {asker} owes
A debt to {creditor}
plea: I promised {creditor} the money {due}. I swore it, before witnesses. I don't have it. I'll lose everything, the house, the trade - everything.
You'll think me a fool. I gave my word to {creditor}, and I can't keep it. {due}, they come for what I owe.
news_lapse: {asker} of {town} is ruined by debt to {creditor}.
In {town}, {creditor} has taken {asker}'s goods for a debt.

note: {rival_full} wants {prize} too, and will not step aside.

label: Let {asker} have it. You have enough.
say: ...Let them have it. I'm tired of the whole business.
Fine. Fine! But they'll owe me.
fail_say: Never. It's mine by right.

label: What would it take for you to step aside?
say: For that? For that, they can have it.

label: Share it between you. Half and half.
say: Half. Half is better than a quarrel to the grave, I suppose.
fail_say: Half? I'd rather burn it.

note: {judge_full} will decide, and listens to whoever speaks best.

label: Let me speak for {asker}.
say: You make a fair case. {asker} shall have it.
Hm. Yes. Yes, that's right. {asker}, then.
fail_say: I'll hear no more of it today.

line: {asker} has {prize}. {rival} does not greet you any more.
{prize} is {asker}'s, and {judge} has said so before the town.
Shared: neither is glad of it, and both are glad it is over.
{asker} and {rival} have half each. They still do not speak.
They quarrelled until {judge} gave {prize} to neither. A cousin from the city has it now.
Both lost it: {judge}, sick of them, gave {prize} to the temple.

prize: the lease of the old mill
a seat at the town's table
the strip of land by the river
the hand of the miller's daughter
title: {asker} and {rival}
Who shall have {prize}
{prize}
plea: {rival} wants {prize}. It should be mine - everyone knows it should be mine. {judge} decides {due}. Speak for me. They'll listen to someone like you.
There's {prize}, and there's two of us that want it, and only one of us deserves it. Help me.

note: {knower_full} knows {asker}'s secret and means to tell it.

label: Keep what you know to yourself. It harms nobody buried.
say: ...Maybe it does no good, telling it. Maybe.
For your sake, then. Not theirs.
fail_say: The truth is the truth. People should know.

label: Here. For your silence.
say: I didn't see a thing. Never did.

label: Say a word of it and you will regret it.
say: I - I won't say anything. I swear it.
fail_say: You don't frighten me. I'll tell it in the market.

label: What is it they know? I cannot help blind.
say: ...Years ago, I did a thing I am ashamed of. A thing that would end me here. {knower} saw.
There was a child, before I married. Nobody knows. {knower} knows.

label: Tell it, then. The town should know.
say: I will. I will, today.

label: I know it too, now. That will cost you.
say: ...How much? Just say how much.
fail_say: Then tell it. I'm done being afraid.

line: It stays buried. {asker} sleeps again.
{knower} will say nothing. {asker} owes you more than coin.
Told: the whole town knows {asker}'s secret. Some are kinder than {asker} feared.
It is out. {asker} keeps indoors, and the street talks of nothing else.
You used it. {asker} pays, and hates you, and will go on paying.
Used: {asker}'s secret is yours now, and so is a little of {asker}'s coin.
{knower} told it in the market. {asker} keeps indoors now.
The secret came out without you. It always does.

title: {asker}'s secret
What {knower} knows
Something buried
plea: {knower} knows something about me. Something old. If it comes out I'm finished in this town. Make it go away. I don't care how.
There is a thing about me nobody must know, and {knower} knows it. Help me keep it buried.
first: {asker} has a secret, and {knower} means to tell it.

truth_to_prove.name: A truth that must be proven

note: {witness_full} heard it, and is afraid to say so.

label: You were there. Say what you heard.
say: ...I heard it. {dead} said it plain: it all goes to {asker}. There. I said it.
Yes. I was there. I'll say it before {judge}, if I must.
fail_say: I saw nothing. I heard nothing.

label: Your time is worth something. Here.
say: ...All right. I'll tell {judge} what I heard.

label: Who are you afraid of?
say: {rival}. I'm afraid of {rival}. But you're here now. All right, I'll tell it.
fail_say: Nobody. Leave me alone.

label: There is a witness. Hear them, and judge.
say: Then it's proven, and that's an end of it. {asker} has the right.

label: Believe {asker}. You know them.
say: ...I believe them. Without proof, mind. People will talk.
fail_say: Bring me proof, or bring me nothing.

line: Proven before {judge}: {asker} has what is theirs.
The witness spoke, {judge} judged, and {rival} has nothing to say.
Believed, without proof. {asker} has it, and the town whispers that {asker} has it unfairly.
{judge} found for {rival}. {asker} has nothing.
Without proof it was lost. {rival} has it all.

title: {dead}'s last words
{asker}'s claim
The proof
stakes: whether {asker} can prove the truth before {judge}
plea: Everyone knows what was promised me. {rival} says it was never said. Somebody heard it - somebody must have. {judge} decides {due}.
It's mine by right, and I can't prove it. Help me prove it, {by_due}, before {judge}.
first: {asker} must prove a truth before {judge}, {by_due}, against {rival}.

note: Someone in {town} knows who really did it.

label: Where were you that night?
say: ...At home. Asleep. Why do you - why are you looking at me like that?
Why does it matter where I was? I - I was nowhere.
note: {culprit} lied about that night. It was {culprit}, not {accused}.
fail_say: At home, like every honest soul.

note: {judge_full} has {accused} to hang {due}.

label: It was {culprit_full}. Here is how I know.
say: ...Then {accused} goes free, and {culprit} answers for it.

label: Spare {accused}. There is no proof.
say: Mercy, then. But the town will have its opinion.
fail_say: The law is the law. {due}.

label: Perhaps a fine would settle it.
say: A fine. Yes. A fine meets the case.

line: {accused} is free, and the town knows it was {culprit}.
Freed, and cleared: {accused} walks home through the square with {asker}.
Freed but shamed: {accused} lives, and the town still whispers.
{accused} is out, and nobody will buy from {asker}'s house for a while.
{accused} is dead. Innocent, and dead.
They hanged {accused} at dawn. {asker} was at the front of the crowd.
{accused} hanged, as was said. Some say {culprit} was in the crowd, and did not look away.

title: {accused} accused
The hanging in {town}
The wrong one
stakes: {accused}, to hang for what {accused_they} did not do
plea: They say {accused} did it. {accused} didn't. I know my own {accused_kin}. They hang {accused_them} {due}. Please. You can ask questions. You can make them listen.
My {accused_kin}... they're going to hang {accused_them}. For nothing. {due}. Please help me.
first: {accused} is to hang {due}; {asker} swears {accused_they} is innocent.
news_lapse: In {town}, {accused} was hanged for a crime.

note: {witness} saw what {culprit} did, and is afraid of {lord}.

label: You saw it. I will stand by you.
say: ...I saw it. It was {culprit}. God help me, I'll say it.
It was {culprit}. Everyone knows, and nobody says.
fail_say: I have children. I saw nothing.

label: Enough coin to leave town, if you must. Now tell me.
say: ...It was {culprit}. I'm going to my sister's tonight.

note: {lord_full} will not judge {lord_their} own {culprit_kin}.

label: Your {culprit_kin} did it, and the town knows. Judge as you would judge any of them.
say: ...So be it. The cells, then. And may the gods forgive me.
fail_say: Get out. Get out of my hall.

label: Make it right with coin, then, if not with justice.
say: Coin. Yes. {asker} will have coin, and an end to it.

line: {lord} judged {lord_their} own {culprit_kin}. {culprit} is in the cells.
Judged: the town saw that the law is for {lord}'s house too.
Paid off: {asker} has coin, and {culprit} has nothing to fear.
{lord} paid {asker}. It is not justice. It is money.
Avenged outside the law: {culprit} is dead, and {lord} will not forget it.
{culprit} is dead. Nobody calls it justice. Nobody calls it murder, either, where {lord} can hear.
Nothing came of it. {culprit} walks the streets as before; {asker} does not. {asker} has left {town}.
{asker} gave up and went away. {culprit} laughs in the inn.

title: {lord}'s {culprit_kin}
What {culprit} did
No justice in {town}
stakes: whether {culprit} answers for it, though {culprit_they} is {lord}'s {culprit_kin}
plea: {culprit} did it. Everyone knows {culprit} did it. But {culprit} is {lord}'s {culprit_kin}, and so nothing happens. Nothing ever happens.
There's no law in {town} for the {lord_title}'s family. Is there any anywhere?

wrong_awaits_revenge.name: A wrong that waits for revenge

label: Let it go. Killing {enemy} will not mend it.
say: ...Maybe not. Maybe nothing mends it.
I'll let it be. For now. For you.
fail_say: You don't know what they did.

label: Pay {asker} for the wrong, and there is an end of it.
say: If coin ends it, coin it is. I'm too old for knives in the dark.
fail_say: I owe that one nothing.

label: Take this as the price of it, from me, and let it rest.
say: ...From you? Why would you - all right. All right. It rests.

line: {asker} let it go. {enemy} will never know how near it came.
Stopped: {asker} put the knife away, and slept.
Turned into a price paid: {asker} has coin for the wrong, and an ache where the wrong was.
A price was paid. Nobody died. Nobody forgave, either.
Done: {enemy} is dead, and {asker} paid what was promised, and cannot look at you.
{enemy} is dead. {asker} thought it would feel like more.
{asker} did it at last, with a knife, in the street. The watch took {asker} before the body was cold.
{enemy} is dead, and {asker} is in the cells for it.

title: {asker}'s grudge
What {enemy} owes
Blood for {asker}
plea: {enemy} wronged me, years ago, and has never paid. I want it done. I'll pay you. Or I'll do it myself - and they'll hang me for it.
Somebody has to make {enemy} pay. If it isn't you, it'll be me, and I'll make a mess of it.
first: {asker} wants {enemy} dead for an old wrong.
news_lapse: In {town}, {asker} killed {enemy} for an old wrong.

label: {avenger} means to kill you. Leave town for a while.
say: ...My cousin has a farm three days east. I'll go tonight.
fail_say: Run? From {avenger}? Never.

line: Peace between the houses: the feud is put to rest, for this generation.
{avenger} and {marked} shook hands in the square. The old ones say they never thought to see it.
{marked} is gone from {town}: alive, and not home.
Prevented, for now: {marked} is away, and {avenger} waits.
The feud took its due. {marked} is in the ground.
{marked} is dead, as the feud said {marked_they} would be.
The feud took its due: {avenger} killed {marked} at the well.
{marked} is dead. The next death is already owed.

title: The feud
Blood owed
{avenger}'s due
stakes: {marked}'s life: the feud says {avenger} must kill {marked_them}
the next death of the feud
plea: My {marked_kin}... {avenger} has sworn to kill {marked_them}. It's the feud. It's always the feud. Make it stop.
{avenger}'s family and ours. Three dead already, in my lifetime. {marked} is next. Please.
first: The feud says {avenger} must kill {marked}; {asker} begs for peace.

note: {sick} is sick, and getting worse.
magic_note: Your spell takes. By evening {sick} sits up and asks for bread.

label: Let me see what ails you.
say: ...The well. You think it's the well? We'll draw from the river, then.
It's lighter already. I can breathe.
fail_say: Nobody knows. Nobody knows what it is.

note: {healer} could help, for a price.

label: Come and see {sick}. I will pay.
say: Show me. Ah. Yes. I know this. Boil the water, and this, three times a day.

line: {sick} is well again, and {asker} has found the cause and stopped it.
Cured: {sick} is up and about, thinner, and alive.
{sick} died before it could be stopped.
It spreads: {sick} is dead, and two more in the street are coughing.
{sick} is buried. The sickness is not.

title: {sick}'s sickness
The coughing house
What ails {sick}
stakes: {sick}'s life, and whoever drinks where {sick} drank
plea: {sick} is sick. It started small, and now {sick_they} can't stand. The healer shrugs. It's something in the house, I think - or the water. Help us.
My {sick_kin} is dying, and nobody knows why. Please.
first: {sick} is sick with something that has a cause; {asker} asked for help.

note: Something lies on {asker}'s house: the milk sours, the children cry at night.
magic_note: Your spell takes: the cold goes out of {asker}'s house like a breath let go.

label: Let me look at the signs.
say: ...Those marks on the lintel? My husband's mother scratched them there. She never liked me.
A knot of hair under the step. Who would - oh.
fail_say: It's just bad luck. That's all it is.
note: The curse was laid with old marks on the house; it can be unsaid.

label: Say the words over the door, as the old ones did.
say: The air's different. Can you feel it? It's different.
fail_say: ...It's worse. Gods, it's worse.

note: {priest} would bless the house, for the temple's due.

label: Bless {asker}'s house. I will pay the temple.
say: The gods hear coin as well as prayer. I'll go tonight.

line: Lifted: the milk keeps, the children sleep.
{asker}'s house is clean again. {asker} keeps a candle for you in the window.
The curse is worse for your meddling. {asker} has shut up the house.
Lived with: {asker} hangs iron over the door and does not speak of it.
{asker} has learned to live with it. The house is cold, and they are used to the cold.

title: The curse on {asker}'s house
{asker}'s cold house
A dead hand on the door
stakes: {asker}'s house and everyone under its roof
plea: There's a curse on my house. Don't laugh. The milk sours overnight. The children wake screaming. The dog won't come in. Somebody did this.
Something is wrong with my house. Something was done to it. Can you see these things? Can you undo them?

precious_wrong_hands.name: Something precious in the wrong hands

note: {holder_full} has {heirloom}, and will part with it only for coin.

label: I will buy {heirloom}.
say: Done. A pleasure, as they say.
Coin on the table, and it's yours.

label: It was never yours to keep. Half, and be glad of it.
say: Half. You'd haggle the teeth out of a dog. Take it.
fail_say: The price is the price.

label: Hand it over, or I take it.
say: Take it, then! Take it and get out!
fail_say: Try it. The watch is just outside.

label: I have {heirloom}. Here.
say: Oh. Oh, you found it. You found it.

line: {heirloom} is back where it belongs.
{asker} has {heirloom} again, and holds it as if it might fly away.
Bought back dear: {asker} has {heirloom}, and you are lighter for it.
Returned, at a price. {asker} swears to pay you back. One day.
Lost: {holder} sold {heirloom} on to a trader from the south.
{heirloom} is gone. {asker} had a copy made by the smith; it is not the same.

heirloom: the family's old ring with the green stone
title: {heirloom}
{asker}'s ring
In {holder}'s hands
plea: {holder} has {heirloom}. I pawned it, when times were bad, and now {holder} won't give it back at any price I can pay. It's all I have of them.
{heirloom} - it was stolen, and now it's in {holder}'s window, and {holder} says it was bought fair.

note: {lost} was last seen on the way to {place_site}.

line: Found, and alive: the dead one came home on {lost_their} own feet.
{lost} is home. Everyone had given up but {asker}.
Found dead, and buried: {asker} knows now, and that is something.
You brought back what was left of {lost}. {asker} buried {lost_them} by the temple, and thanked you.
Never found. {asker} stopped asking strangers at the gate.
Nobody went to {place_site}. {lost} is a name now, and a place set at the table.

title: {lost}, missing
The road to {place_site}
Where is {lost}?
plea: {lost} went out to {place_site} and never came back. Everyone says {lost_they}'s dead. If {lost_they} is, bring {lost_them} home so I can bury {lost_them}. If not... bring {lost_them} home.
My {lost_kin} is lost. Out by {place_site}. Find {lost_them}, living or dead. I have to know.

love_not_to_be.name: A love that must not be

note: {elder_full} will not hear of {asker} and {beloved}.

label: Give them your blessing. You will lose {asker} otherwise.
say: ...I would rather have a {asker_kin} than be right. Tell them. Tell them yes.
Fine. Fine. Let them marry. Let them be happy, if they can.
fail_say: Over my grave.

label: If it is a matter of a dowry, I will give it.
say: ...Well. With a dowry like that, nobody can say a word against it.

label: Then go together. Tonight, by the back road.
say: Tonight. Yes. Tonight.

line: Together: {asker} and {beloved} are married at the temple door, and {elder} weeps at the back.
{asker} and {beloved} are wed. {elder} came, in the end.
Fled together, outlawed in the eyes of their families.
{asker} and {beloved} were gone by morning. {elder} has burned everything {asker} left behind.
Parted: {beloved} was sent away to kin in another town.
{elder} won. {beloved} is gone, and {asker} goes to the temple every day and says nothing.

title: {asker} and {beloved}
A love that must not be
{elder}'s word
stakes: {asker} and {beloved}, and whether {elder} will let them be
plea: I love {beloved}. {elder} says I'll marry {beloved} over {elder_their} dead body - that I'll marry who I'm told. Help us. Or help us go.
{elder} has found out about {beloved} and me. {elder} wants me married to someone else {by_due}.

note: {band} have {child} at {band_site}, for ransom.
{child} is held at {band_site} by {band}.

label: Pay them. I will give you the ransom.
say: ...They took it. They let {child_them} go at the crossroads. {child} is home.

line: Saved: {child} is home, and asleep in {asker}'s lap before the fire is lit.
{child} is home. {asker} cannot speak; {asker} only holds on.
Saved at a price: {band} have your coin, and will take another child when they need more.
{child} is home, bought back. {band} are richer.
Lost: {child} is dead.
Lost: {band} moved on, and took {child} with them.
Nobody paid, and nobody went. {child} is gone, sold, they say, in the south.

title: {child}
Taken by {band}
{asker}'s {child_kin}
plea: They took {child}. {band}. They want more than I've ever seen in my life, {by_due}, or... or I don't know. I don't know what they'll do.
My {child_kin}. {child} is only small. {band} have {child_them} at {band_site}.
news_lapse: A child of {town} was taken by {band} and not returned.

stranger_not_himself.name: The stranger is not who he says

note: {stranger_full} is not who {stranger_they} says.

label: Your name. Your real one.
say: ...Keep your voice down. It isn't {stranger}. It hasn't been for a long time.
You're sharper than the rest. All right. Not here. But you're right.
fail_say: {stranger}. As I said.

label: I know who you are. Soon everyone will.
say: ...What do you want? Just tell me what you want.
fail_say: Then you know more than I do.

label: I found out who {stranger} is.
say: I knew it. I knew it. The watch will have a word with {stranger_them}.

label: {stranger} is harmless. Leave it be.
say: If you say so. You've been right before.
fail_say: You're lying for them. Why?

label: They are asking about you. Go, while you can.
say: ...Thank you. I won't forget it.

line: Unmasked: {stranger} is in the watch's hands, and {asker} sleeps easier.
{asker} has the truth about {stranger}, and so does the watch.
Protected: {stranger} stays, and owes you a secret.
{stranger} keeps {stranger_their} false name, and sends you word now and then.
Let go: {stranger} left before dawn, and nobody in {town} will ever know who {stranger_they} was.
The stranger left one night, owing for the room.
{stranger} is gone, and whoever {stranger_they} was went too.

title: {stranger}
The stranger at the inn
Who is {stranger}?
stakes: the truth about the stranger who calls {stranger_them}self {stranger}
plea: There's a stranger at the inn calls {stranger_them}self {stranger}. Says {stranger_they}'s a {stranger_title}. {stranger_they} isn't. Find out what {stranger_they} is, before something happens.
I don't like {stranger}. Nobody comes to {town} for nothing. Find out who {stranger_they} is.
first: {asker} wants to know who the stranger {stranger} really is.

note: The watch is searching every house for {fugitive}.

label: I saw someone running for the river road. That way.
say: The river road? Right. Thank you, traveller.
fail_say: Funny. Nobody else saw anyone.

label: Search somewhere else. Here.
say: I'll search the other end of town. Slowly.

label: {fugitive} is hiding at {asker}'s.
say: Is that so. Right, lads.

label: Now. Out by the back way, and don't stop.
say: I won't forget this. Tell my {asker_kin}...

line: Away free: {fugitive} is over the hills, and the watch is still searching the river road.
{fugitive} got away. {asker} will hide you, one day, if you need it.
Handed over: {fugitive} is in the cells, and {asker} will spit when you pass.
You gave {fugitive} to the watch. The reward is in your purse.
Caught: the watch found {fugitive} in {asker}'s loft.
{fugitive} is in the cells. {asker} sits outside them every day.

title: {fugitive} in hiding
The search
The watch at {asker}'s door
stakes: {fugitive}, hidden in {asker}'s house, and the watch searching
plea: {fugitive} ran from the levy. {fugitive}'s hiding in my house. The watch are going door to door. If they find {fugitive_them}, they hang {fugitive_them}. Get {fugitive_them} out of town.
You have to help me. {fugitive} is in the loft and the watch are two doors down.
news_lapse: {town}'s watch caught {fugitive}, who was in hiding.

line: Served: the letter came where it was going, and {asker} remembers who carried it.
{asker}'s need was met. Doors in {town} open a little wider for you.
Served badly: the letter came late, or not at all.
Refused, and remembered: {asker} does not ask twice.
The letter went with another rider. {asker} remembers who would not carry it.

title: {asker}'s letter
A letter for {envoy_to}
The {asker_title}'s need
plea: I have need of someone who can ride and fight and keep their mouth shut. A letter, to {envoy_to_full}. It must arrive, and nobody must read it.
I need a letter carried to {envoy_to_full}. My own riders are watched. You are not.

rite_to_be_done.name: A rite that must be done

note: {priest_full} will not say the rite for {dead}.

label: The gods are not so small. Say the words.
say: ...You know the old books. Perhaps you are right. I will say it.
Hm. There is a precedent. Very well.
fail_say: You know nothing of the gods.

label: For the temple's roof, then. Say the words.
say: The roof does leak. The gods will understand.

label: Do it for {asker}, if not for the dead.
say: ...For {asker}. Yes.
fail_say: My hands are tied.

label: Then we will say the words ourselves. I will help.
say: It was not right. It was not the priest. But it was something.
fail_say: I can't. I can't do it without the priest.

line: Done: the rite is said over {dead}, and {asker} can grieve.
{priest} said the words. {dead} rests, and {asker} with {dead}.
Done wrong: the words were said, but not by a priest, and the old women of {town} shake their heads.
Not done, and the omen: a crow sat on {asker}'s roof for three days, and the town says it was {dead}.
No rite was said. {asker} sees {dead} in dreams, every night.

title: The rite for {dead}
{dead}, unshriven
No words for {dead}
stakes: whether {dead} is laid to rest as the gods ask
plea: {priest} won't say the words over {dead}. Because of how {dead} lived, {priest} says. If the rite isn't said {by_due}... you know what they say happens.
The rite. {dead} must have the rite, and {priest} refuses. Speak to {priest}. Please.
first: {priest} will not say the rite for {dead}; {asker} needs it done {by_due}.
news_lapse: In {town}, the dead went without their rite, and folk talk of omens.

note: The dead walk by {asker}'s house at night, and will not rest until what was taken is brought back from {place_site}.
magic_note: Your spell takes. The cold by the door is gone; it is held, if not laid.

label: Tell me what the dead one wants.
say: It's the old one's things. Taken from the grave by thieves and hidden out at {place_site}. That's what it wants.
It says one word, over and over: {place_site}.
fail_say: I don't know what it wants! That's the horror of it.

line: Laid: what was taken is back in the grave, and the nights in {town} are only nights.
The dead rest. {asker} sleeps with the shutters open for the first time in a month.
Bound, not laid: it is quiet now, and the old ones say it is waiting.
Angered: it broke the shutters on {asker}'s house, and {asker}'s family sleep at the temple now.
The dead did not rest. Now nobody in {asker}'s street does.

title: What walks by {asker}'s door
The restless dead
The thing at the window
stakes: {asker}'s house, and the dead who walk by it
the rest of the dead, and of {asker}
plea: Something comes to my window at night. It was a person once. It wants something - I think it wants what was taken from its grave. Out at {place_site}, the old men say.
The dead are walking. Mine, by my house. I have not slept in a week. Please.
first: The dead walk by {asker}'s house; what they want is out at {place_site}.
